 Information about HP Inc.'s use of non-GAAP financial information is provided under "Use of non-GAAP financial information" below. | Net revenue and EPS results 
 HP Inc. and its subsidiaries (“HP” or the "Company") announced fiscal 2026 net revenue of $60.5 billion, up 9.5% (up 7.8% in constant currency) from the prior-year period. 
 Fiscal 2026 GAAP diluted net EPS was $2.62, down from $2.65 in the prior-year and within the previously provided outlook of $2.52 to $2.62. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted net EPS was $3.33, up from $3.12 in the prior-year and above the previously provided outlook of $3.19 to $3.29. Both GAAP and non-GAAP diluted net EPS included a $0.26 favorable impact from tariff refunds, as compared to the $0.19 impact included in the previously provided outlook. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP net earnings and non-GAAP diluted net EPS exclude certain adjustments. Refer to "Adjustments to GAAP Net earnings" section in the below tables. 
 Fourth quarter net revenue was $16.0 billion, up 9.3% (up 8.6% in constant currency) from the prior-year period. 
 Fourth quarter GAAP diluted net EPS was $0.84, flat from $0.84 in the prior-year period and within the previously provided outlook of $0.74 to $0.84. Fourth quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS was $0.83, down from $0.93 in the prior-year period and above the previously provided outlook of $0.69 to $0.79. Both GAAP and non-GAAP diluted net EPS included a $0.15 favorable impact from tariff refunds, as compared to the $0.08 impact included in the previously provided outlook. Fourth quarter non-GAAP net earnings and non-GAAP diluted net EPS exclude certain adjustments. Refer to "Adjustments to GAAP Net earnings" section in the below tables. 
 “In the fourth quarter, we continued to grow our higher-value businesses, with AI PCs reaching nearly 60% of shipments, while taking steps to address memory and storage cost pressures,” said Bruce Broussard, Interim CEO, HP Inc. “Advances in processing power and engineering are accelerating AI at the edge, enabling agentic experiences and new device form factors. We believe these innovations will drive multiple waves of device refresh and create sustained growth opportunities. With our engineering expertise, global scale, and deep customer relationships, HP is uniquely positioned to help define the next era of edge computing and create long-term value for customers and shareholders." 
 “We grew FY26 revenue 9.5%, delivered on our guidance for the year, exceeded our free cash flow target and returned $2.3 billion to shareholders, despite a challenging environment,” said Karen Parkhill, CFO, HP Inc. “While our fiscal 2027 outlook reflects a prudent view of continued cost and demand pressures, we have a strong track record of addressing challenges and are confident in our ability to drive improvement in our profitability throughout the year.” | Asset management 
 HP generated $4.0 billion in net cash provided by operating activities and $3.3 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Free cash flow includes net cash provided by operating activities of $4.0 billion adjusted for net investment in leases from integrated financing of $142 million and net investments in property, plant, equipment and purchased intangibles of $0.8 billion. HP utilized $1.2 billion of cash during fiscal 2026 to repurchase approximately 46.7 million shares of common stock in the open market. When combined with the $1.1 billion of cash used to pay 
 dividends, HP returned 70% of its free cash flow to shareholders in fiscal 2026. 
 HP's net cash provided by operating activities in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $0.9 billion. Accounts receivable ended the quarter at $7.0 billion, down 2 days quarter over quarter to 39 days. Inventory ended the quarter at $12.3 billion, up 11 days quarter over quarter to 84 days. Accounts payable ended the quarter at $22.7 billion, up 4 days quarter over quarter to 155 days. 
 HP generated $0.8 billion of free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Free cash flow includes net cash provided by operating activities of $0.9 billion adjusted for net investment in leases from integrated financing of $73 million and net investments in property, plant, equipment and purchased intangibles of $201 million. 
 HP’s dividend payment of $0.30 per share in the fourth quarter resulted in cash usage of $270 million. HP also utilized $0.5 billion of cash during the quarter to repurchase approximately 15.9 million shares of common stock in the open market. HP exited the quarter with $4.4 billion in gross cash, which includes cash and cash equivalents of $4.4 billion, restricted cash of $2 million, and short-term investments of $3 million included in other current assets. Restricted cash is related to amounts collected and held on behalf of a third party for trade receivables previously sold. 
 The HP board of directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.31 per share on the Company’s common 
 stock, payable on January 6, 2027 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 9, 2026. 
 This is the first dividend of HP's 2027 fiscal year. 
 Fiscal 2026 fourth quarter segment results 
 Personal Systems net revenue was $11.8 billion, up 14% year over year (up 13% in constant currency) with a 3.0% operating margin. Consumer PS net revenue was down 7% and Commercial PS net revenue was up 23%. Total units were down 29% with Consumer PS units down 31% and Commercial PS units down 28%. 
 Printing net revenue was $4.3 billion, down 1% year over year (down 2% in constant currency) with a 19.7% operating margin. Consumer Printing net revenue was down 1% and Commercial Printing net revenue was up 2%. Supplies net revenue was down 2% (down 3% in constant currency). Total hardware units were down 2%, with Consumer Printing units down 3% and Commercial Printing units down 1%. | Stock-Based Compensation Expense Change 
 Effective starting the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, HP will exclude stock-based compensation expense from non-GAAP cost of net revenue, gross profit, gross margin, operating expenses, earnings from operations, operating margin, net earnings and diluted net EPS. HP will reflect this change to the prior periods presented on an as-if basis and this change will have no impact on the Company's previously reported consolidated GAAP results. With this change the Company expects a non-GAAP tax rate of 17% based on current tax laws. The net impact of this change would be $0.38 per share in fiscal year 2026. | Outlook 
 For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, HP estimates non-GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $0.66 to $0.76. Fiscal 2027 first quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimates excludes $0.24 primarily related to restructuring and other charges, amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense and corresponding tax impacts. Other than these known adjustments, certain items such as certain litigation charges (benefits) and tax adjustments cannot be reasonably estimated or predicted or is dependent on future events outside of our control and reconciliation is not available without unreasonable effort. 
 For fiscal 2027, HP estimates non-GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $3.15 to $3.45. Fiscal 2027 non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimates excludes $0.75 primarily related to restructuring and other charges, amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense and corresponding tax impacts. Other than these known adjustments, certain items such as certain litigation charges (benefits) and tax adjustments cannot be reasonably estimated or predicted or is dependent on future events outside of our control and reconciliation is not available without unreasonable effort. 
 For fiscal 2027, HP estimates free cash flow to be in the range of $2.9 to $3.1 billion. 
 More information on HP's earnings, including additional financial analysis and an earnings overview presentation, is available on HP's Investor Relations website at https://investor.hp.com . 
 HP's FY26 Q4 earnings conference call is accessible via audio webcast at www.hp.com/investor/2026Q4Webcast . | About HP Inc. 
 HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ) is a global technology leader redefining the Future of Work. Operating in more than 180 countries, HP delivers innovative and AI-powered devices, software, services and subscriptions that drive business growth and professional fulfillment. For more information, please visit https://www.hp.com .

the protection of HP’s intellectual property assets, including intellectual property licensed from third parties; disruptions in operations from system security risks, data protection breaches, or cyberattacks; our aspirations related to environmental and societal matters; potential impacts, liabilities and costs from pending or potential investigations, claims and disputes; | the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting; and other risks that are described in HP’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended October 31, 2025 and HP’s other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). HP’s fiscal 2026 plan includes HP’s efforts to drive customer satisfaction, product innovation, and productivity primarily through artificial intelligence adoption and enablement, and the resulting efficiencies, including those that enable a reduction in workforce. Anticipated cost savings associated with the fiscal 2026 plan represent expected gross reductions in costs from these measures. These cost savings are net of any new recurring costs resulting from these initiatives and exclude one-time investments to generate such savings. HP’s expectations on the longer-term sustainability of such cost savings are based on its current business operations and market dynamics and could be significantly impacted by various factors, including but not limited to HP’s evolving business models, future investment decisions, market environment and technology landscape. 
 As in prior periods, the financial information set forth in this document, including any tax-related items, reflects estimates based on information available at this time.
